Indian Railways plan: double originating train capacity in 48 major cities by 2030. Part of infrastructure expansion. ~₹2.4 lakh crore investment.
Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?
Palk Strait: ~53-80 km. Separates Tamil Nadu from northern Sri Lanka. Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu).
The August Offer was made by:
August Offer (August 1940, Linlithgow): promised dominion status after war. Rejected by Congress.
Who was the founder of the Mauryan Empire?
Chandragupta Maurya (322-298 BCE): founded Mauryan Empire with Chanakya's help.

Cabinet Mission (March 1946): Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps, Alexander. Proposed federal India, Constituent Assembly.

Brahmaputra: Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet. Enters India through Arunachal Pradesh (Dihang). Joins Ganga in Bangladesh.

106th Amendment (September 2023): 1/3rd reservation for women in Lok Sabha + state assemblies. 15-year implementation. Introduced in new Parliament.
The longest wall in the world is:
Great Wall of China: ~21,000 km. Built over centuries (7th century BCE - 17th century CE). UNESCO World Heritage.
The Zojila Pass connects which two regions?

Hockey: traditionally considered national sport (8 Olympic golds). However, govt says no official national sport. Cricket most popular.
Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on:
Jallianwala Bagh (13 April 1919, Baisakhi): Brig. Dyer fired on peaceful gathering at Amritsar. 379+ killed. Rabindranath Tagore returned knighthood.
How many fundamental rights are guaranteed by the Indian Constitution?
6 fundamental rights (Articles 12-35): Equality, Freedom, Against Exploitation, Religion, Cultural/Educational, Constitutional Remedies. Right to Property removed (44th Amendment, 1978).
Which is the longest beach in India?

Which gas is most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
Atmosphere: Nitrogen 78%, Oxygen 21%, Argon 0.93%, CO2 0.04%. Nitrogen: inert, prevents rapid oxidation.
Which is the longest river in the world?
Nile (~6650 km): traditionally considered longest. Flows through 11 African countries. Amazon: largest by discharge (disputed longest).

The Tropic of Capricorn is at which latitude?
Tropic of Capricorn: 23.5°S (Southern Hemisphere). Tropic of Cancer: 23.5°N (Northern Hemisphere).

Caspian Sea: largest lake (~371,000 sq km). Saline. Surrounded by 5 countries (Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan).

Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Educational Guarantee Act

MGNREGA (2005): 100 days of wage employment per rural household per year. Legal right. ~15 crore active workers. Largest social security program globally.
Which is the highest mountain peak in India?
Kanchenjunga (8586m): 3rd highest in world. On Sikkim-Nepal border. India's highest (K2 in PoK disputed). First climbed 1955.
The longest river in South India is:
Godavari: 1465 km. Longest in South India. 'Dakshin Ganga'. Origin: Trimbakeshwar (Maharashtra).
The first Anglo-Mysore War ended with which treaty?
1st Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69): Haidar Ali vs British. Treaty of Madras (1769): status quo ante. British promised help if attacked (didn't fulfill).

Who is known as the 'Father of Economics'?
Adam Smith: 'Father of Economics'. 'The Wealth of Nations' (1776). Concept of 'invisible hand' (free market).
The chemical formula for water is:
Water: H₂O. 2 hydrogen + 1 oxygen. Covers ~71% of Earth's surface. Essential for life.

Kunchikal Falls (Karnataka, ~455m): highest in India. On Varahi river. Jog Falls (253m): 2nd highest.
Who was the last Mughal Emperor?
Bahadur Shah Zafar (1775-1862): last Mughal emperor. Exiled to Rangoon after 1857 revolt. Wrote 'Lagta nahin hai dil mera'.

First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46): British defeated Sikhs. Treaty of Lahore (1846): Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh for ₹75 lakh.
The 'Curzon Line' is the boundary between:
Curzon Line: proposed by Lord Curzon (1919) as Poland-Soviet border. Became permanent after WWII. ~384 km. Named after British Foreign Secretary (not Viceroy).
The Permanent Settlement was introduced by:
Permanent Settlement (1793, Cornwallis): in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa. Fixed land revenue. Made zamindars hereditary owners. Failed experiment.
The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in:
Non-Cooperation (September 1920): Gandhi. Boycott of schools, courts, foreign goods. Withdrawn after Chauri Chaura (1922).

Mitochondria: 'powerhouse of cell'. Produces ATP via cellular respiration (Krebs cycle, ETC). Has own DNA (endosymbiotic theory).

Wavell Plan (1945, Shimla Conference): proposed Executive Council with Indian members. Failed (Jinnah demanded Muslim veto).

'Neither' is singular → 'has' (not 'have'). Correct: 'Neither of the two boys has completed...'
Bibliophile: lover of books. From Greek 'biblion' (book) + 'philos' (loving).
Change to passive: 'She writes a letter.'
A letter has been written by her.
A letter was written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
A letter is written by her.
Active 'writes' (simple present) → Passive 'is written'. Subject: a letter. Agent: by her.
Diligent: showing care + effort. Synonyms: hardworking, industrious, meticulous.
'No point in' + V-ing. 'No point in arguing.'
Change to indirect: 'He said, "I am reading a book."'
He said that he is reading a book.
He said that he was reading a book.
He said that he had read a book.
He said that he had been reading a book.
Present continuous 'am reading' → past continuous 'was reading' (backshift).
Burn the midnight oil: work or study late into the night.
A penny for your thoughts: asking what someone is thinking about.
Philanthropist: lover of mankind. From Greek 'philos' (love) + 'anthropos' (man).
Change to indirect: 'He said, "I will go tomorrow."'
He said that he will go tomorrow.
He said that he would go tomorrow.
He said that he would go the next day.
He said that he goes tomorrow.
Augment: make larger. Synonyms: increase, enlarge, expand, supplement.
Ardent: showing great enthusiasm or passion. Synonyms: passionate, fervent, zealous.
Fill: 'He has been working _____ he was a child.'
'Since' + point in time (since he was a child). 'For' + duration (for 20 years).
Find the error: 'I am living in this house since 2010.'
Should be present perfect continuous: 'have been living' (for ongoing action since past).
If a passage mentions 'empirical evidence,' what does 'empirical' mean?
Empirical: based on observation, experience, or experiment. Not theoretical or speculative.
Ostentatious: characterized by vulgar/pretentious display. Synonyms: flashy, pretentious, flamboyant.
Passive voice of 'Someone stole my bicycle':
Active 'stole' (simple past) → Passive 'was stolen'. Agent 'someone' can be omitted.
Fill: 'The cat is hiding _____ the table.'
Vegetarian (human): doesn't eat meat. Herbivore (animal): plant-eating.
A blessing in disguise: something that seems bad but turns out to be good.
'Look forward to' + V-ing. 'Look forward to seeing you.'
